transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Reeves (CTO - Stratos), Priya Shah (Cloud Architect), Liam O'Connor (Head of Security), Eva Morales (Infra Engineer)

Summary (auto): quick intake on private/VPC deployment readiness, regional gating, and egress/IP constraints; next steps include network diagram, security pack, and lab benchmark.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex on the Redwood team, and with me is Sofia. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Mark Reeves: Good, thanks. Running a bit behind but ready.
[00:16] Priya Shah: Hi all. We're excited to get into the private deployment options.
[00:23] Sofia Patel: Quick agenda — understand your network posture, region constraints, compliance needs, then map out a safe onramp for private access. Does that sound right?
[00:31] Liam O'Connor: Yep, and we need specifics on encryption / KMS and audit logs. SOC2 is baseline for us.
[00:38] Alex Chen: Totally. We can run through how Redwood Private exposes private endpoints, options for VPC peering, and the Dedicated reserved pools if you need strict throughput plus isolation.
[00:49] Eva Morales: One big constraint: we can't allow any public egress from our inference VPC — all traffic must go via our egress appliances. Also, low-latency to our NYX region is important.
[01:02] Sofia Patel: Noted. Can you describe your current network topology? VPCs, transit gateway, any existing peering?
[01:12] Priya Shah: We have a hub-and-spoke with a transit gateway in us-east-1 (NYX). Spokes in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Some legacy peering to analytics VPCs. We want Redwood to sit in a dedicated spoke or behind a private endpoint.
[01:27] Alex Chen: Ok. Two common patterns: 1) VPC peering from your spoke directly to our Private VPC endpoints, or 2) PrivateLink-style interface endpoints where you bring an ENI into your VPC. For strict egress controls, PrivateLink often helps.
[01:46] Mark Reeves: Do you support AWS PrivateLink or is it just peering?
[01:51] Sofia Patel: We support both patterns. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is the recommended pattern when you need to keep everything private and avoid cross-account route table changes. Peering is simpler but has more IP planning overhead.
[02:04] Liam O'Connor: How about transit gateway attachments? We prefer central management via transit gateway rather than a bunch of individual peering links.
[02:11] Sofia Patel: Transit gateway is fine. We can accept attachments from your TGW — you typically attach a spoke that routes to our endpoint. We just need NACL/security group and route table alignment. There's an ops checklist we can share.
[02:25] Eva Morales: Also region gating — we have a data residency rule: all PII-labeled workloads must stay in eu-west-1. Can Redwood host private endpoints in multiple regions?
[02:35] Alex Chen: Yes. With Redwood Private we can provision control plane and dataplane in specific regions. For hosted customers, we steer requests to regional endpoints; for Private we deploy the inference plane in the selected region(s).
[02:49] Priya Shah: Great. Latency numbers matter. Can you share typical p95 for generation and embedding calls from eu-west-1?
[02:56] Sofia Patel: For a mid-sized LLM with 1k context we see p95 token latency ~120–180ms in-region on our optimized serving runtime. If you need <100ms we recommend smaller context lengths or a dedicated pool sized for low-concurrency.
[03:14] Mark Reeves: Any change to model behavior with quantization / CPU vs GPU? Our compliance folks worry about quality regressions.
[03:21] Alex Chen: We validate quality with per-model evals. Quantization can change outputs slightly — we usually recommend 8-bit quantization and run a brief eval suite. Redwood Optimize offers suggested quant profiles.
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: On encryption, we require customer-managed keys (CMKs) for model artifacts and request logs. Does Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[03:46] Sofia Patel: Yes, Private supports KMS integration and customer-managed keys. For hosted there's a separate key management path but we can also work with HSM-based solutions via partner integrations.
[03:58] Eva Morales: Are audit logs shipped to our splunk or do you provide an S3 export?
[04:04] Alex Chen: We can stream audit logs to your S3 or into SIEMs via Kinesis/Firehose. We'll include sample CloudTrail-compatible events in the security pack.
[04:16] Mark Reeves: Network-wise, what's required from our side to establish peering? IP ranges, allowed ingress, and any NAT considerations?
[04:25] Sofia Patel: We'll need a small set of reserved CIDRs for the interface endpoints, the expected egress IPs if you plan to whitelist, and the route tables to ensure return traffic paths. For no-public-egress setups, you can route our endpoints through your egress appliance; we just need connectivity.
[04:42] Priya Shah: Our proxy requires TLS mutual auth for any inbound services. Can Redwood support mTLS for the control plane?
[04:50] Sofia Patel: We have TLS support and can negotiate mTLS for private deployments; it is a configuration step with cert exchange. We'll put the exact cert formats in the checklist.
[04:59] Eva Morales: Ops question — how do we handle key rotation without downtime?
[05:04] Alex Chen: We support rolling key rotations and zero-downtime certificate swaps using dual-key acceptance windows on Private. We'll detail the rotation process in the security docs.
[05:15] Liam O'Connor: Any extra network cost considerations for cross-region traffic?
[05:20] Sofia Patel: Yes, cross-region traffic between your VPCs and our region will incur cloud egress charges. If you colocate in a region where you have the bulk of traffic — e.g., eu-west-1 — that minimizes inter-region egress.
[05:33] Mark Reeves: On the compliance front, we need an attestation that logs are tamper-evident and retention controls exist for 7 years for specific audits.
[05:41] Alex Chen: Redwood's audit logs support retention policies and WORM-like S3 archive options. For formal attestation, we'll pass along our SOC2 report and a letter describing retention capabilities.
[05:53] Priya Shah: Let's get practical: what's the minimal connectivity sequence to test?
[05:59] Sofia Patel: Minimal path: provision a test spoke in your us-east-1 TGW, create a mock VPC or use a sandbox subnet, accept a PrivateLink interface endpoint, then run a simple token-generation test. We'll provide a small client and a postman collection.
[06:16] Eva Morales: We want to run a load test to validate autoscaling behavior — how do you provision dedicated GPU pools for Private?
[06:24] Alex Chen: For Private we deploy a dedicated inference cluster in your region. Autoscaling policies can be managed by Redwood or delegated to you. For load tests we can pre-warm with reserved capacity. We'll coordinate the exact instance types and GPU counts during the lab booking.
[06:39] Mark Reeves: Can Redwood run inside our account fully, or does it require cross-account resources?
[06:46] Sofia Patel: We have two deployment models: 1) cross-account managed by Redwood (control plane in Redwood account, data plane in customer VPC via PrivateLink) and 2) fully customer-managed on-premises or in-customer account where all resources are in your account. Both are options.
[07:01] Priya Shah: For the fully customer-managed variant, who handles OS/hypervisor patches on the inference hosts?
[07:06] Alex Chen: If it's fully customer-managed, your infra team applies patches. Redwood provides hardened AMIs and a patching schedule we recommend; we can share automation playbooks.
[07:19] Liam O'Connor: We need to ensure we can pass an internal pen test. Is there a sandbox for security testing?
[07:25] Sofia Patel: Yes, we offer a pen test sandbox and a review timeline. We'll need a test plan ahead of time to scope it.
[07:35] Mark Reeves: Any blockers that you've seen commonly derail deployments?
[07:38] Sofia Patel: Common gotchas are IP overlap in peering, strict egress policies that block return traffic, and mistaken assumptions about cross-account role permissions. We try to catch these in the intake checklist.
[07:54] Priya Shah: Ok, let's talk about routing specifics — we use 10.0.0.0/16 for the hub, spokes are /20. Is it okay to carve a /24 for Redwood endpoints?
[08:05] Sofia Patel: Yes a /24 works fine for interface endpoints; we typically recommend non-overlapping subnets and avoiding RFC1918 conflicts with our supplied ranges if we do peering.
[08:15] Eva Morales: How do you handle TLS certificates for mutual auth — do you accept custom CAs?
[08:20] Alex Chen: We accept custom CAs for mTLS. We'll coordinate a CA chain import during onboarding.
[08:29] Mark Reeves: We're also considering Dedicated reserved capacity instead of Private because of throughput needs. What's the difference operationally for networking?
[08:38] Sofia Patel: Dedicated is about reserved GPU capacity; networking is similar if you pick Private deployment — Dedicated can be combined with Private (dedicated pool in your VPC). Hosted Dedicated means reserved capacity in Redwood-managed network; Private Dedicated means both dedicated compute and customer-managed network.
[08:58] Priya Shah: That helps. For the lab test, we want to validate p95 < 150ms for embeddings across eu-west-1. Can you commit to that as a goal?
[09:09] Sofia Patel: We'll target that in the lab. We can instrument tracing and provide latency breakdowns per-token and per-network hop.
[09:20] Eva Morales: One more Q — do you need our VPC to have internet access for control plane callbacks?
[09:26] Alex Chen: If you choose cross-account managed control plane, no public egress is required; control plane runs in Redwood but communicates over PrivateLink. If fully customer-managed, you might need restricted egress for OS updates and metrics streams unless you mirror them internally.
[09:44] Mark Reeves: Right. Let's map owners: Priya will own the cloud prep, Eva will run the infra side, Liam will review security posture.
[09:52] Priya Shah: Correct. We'll also need details for our procurement team — license model, run rates, and SLA commitments.
[09:59] Alex Chen: I'll include a pricing matrix and SLA summary. Sofia will include the technical checklist.
[10:06] Sofia Patel: I'll also attach an example route table and NACL snippet.
[10:12] Mark Reeves: Can you also list expected IPs we might need to whitelist for initial smoke tests?
[10:17] Alex Chen: Yes — for the smoke test we'll provide the ephemeral egress IPs; for production we'll provide stable ranges.
[10:23] Liam O'Connor: One small note — we have a legal requirement to disable third-party telemetry for EU workloads unless approved. How intrusive is Redwood's telemetry?
[10:33] Sofia Patel: Telemetry is configurable. For Private, you can disable app-level telemetry and only forward logs you allow. We can also host telemetry in your SIEM.
[10:44] Priya Shah: Ok, let's go over a tentative timeline: procurement + contracts in 4 weeks, lab in 6 weeks?
[10:52] Alex Chen: That seems feasible. We'll target a lab window in mid-December pending procurement.
[10:58] Eva Morales: Any sample templates for the procurement side?
[11:02] Alex Chen: We'll include a commercial term sheet and an example MSA in the packet.
[11:08] Mark Reeves: For the lab, can we include a small canary app hitting the inference endpoint via our private API gateway?
[11:15] Sofia Patel: Yes, that works. We'll provide a sample canary client and a perf harness.
[11:21] Priya Shah: Regarding model versioning and rollouts — do you support canary rollouts inside Private?
[11:27] Alex Chen: Yes, we support canary and A/B rollouts; SDK features allow pinning and traffic splitting.
[11:33] Liam O'Connor: Anything else to call out?
[11:36] Sofia Patel: I'll summarize the intake checklist items: network diagram, allowed egress list, certs for mTLS if used, region selection, and compliance docs request.
[11:49] Mark Reeves: That sounds good.
[11:52] Alex Chen: Quick recap of next steps: Sofia sends the technical checklist and draft VPC diagram; I send pricing and SLA; Mark/Team to provide egress list and pick lab dates.
[12:05] Priya Shah: We'll aim to have the egress list and timeline by next week.
[12:09] Eva Morales: One last operational question — do you maintain a DR plan for private deployments?
[12:16] Sofia Patel: Yes, multi-AZ redundancy is standard, and we can set up multi-region failover if you require it; we'll include RTO/RPO targets in the docs.
[12:29] Mark Reeves: Perfect. Thanks, everyone.
[12:33] Alex Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up end of day with the packet.
[12:37] Priya Shah: Appreciate it.
[12:40] (call ends)

Note about transcript: occasional speaker overlap and small transcription errors present (e.g., NYX region may be mis-transcribed in some places).
